title: eval harness: add CI prompt-regression gating + telemetry integration
author: Aisha Khan
description: Motivation: reduce silent regressions caused by prompt-set drift and ensure shipping changes that affect prompts or model candidate outputs are blocked until eval metrics meet our quality thresholds. This PR adds a CI hook that runs the eval-harness prompt-set regression checks on changed prompt sets and model config deltas, wires eval metrics back into CI as a gating signal, and exposes a short-circuit flag for opt-out in emergency releases. Summary of changes: add a new GitHub Actions workflow that triggers on PRs touching eval prompt sets or model bindings, implement a lightweight runner that pulls the baseline eval artifacts and compares key metrics, add configurable thresholds and pass/fail reasons to the gating logic, integrate telemetry to reporting_integration so CI reports an aggregated metrics panel in the build UI, and add unit + integration tests and docs. Checklist: 1) add CI workflow (done), 2) implement gate runner and threshold config (done), 3) add telemetry integration for CI UI (done), 4) unit + integration tests (done, flaky e2e retried once), 5) docs + migration notes (done). Testing: locally ran eval-harness suite against sample prompts; initial e2e failed due to timeout on a long-running eval job, re-run with increased timeout and it passed. Also exercised the opt-out flag and the fallback path that posts a warning comment instead of failing when the gate is disabled for a release branch. Related work: ENG-4512 (prompt set regression infra) and ENG-4601 (eval metrics schema). Notes: gating thresholds live in eval-harness/configs/default_gate.yaml and can be overridden per repo via .github/eval-gate.yaml. This PR intentionally keeps the default gate conservative to avoid blocking exploratory changes. If you want to test the gate manually, use scripts/ci/run_eval_gate.sh with --baseline and --candidate flags.
